title: Ezekiel 48:1–7
context: The Lord GOD continues speaking to the prophet, listing the tribal portions from the north: Dan, Asher, Naphtali, Manasseh, Ephraim, Reuben, and Judah, each receiving “one portion” in a strip running from east to west; the arrangement differs from the earlier allotment in Joshua, with every tribe west of the Jordan and in equal shares. Readers in both traditions take the temple vision of chapters 40–48 in the ways named at 40:1–16: as a plan for a literal future temple, as a symbolic or ideal picture of God dwelling with his people, or as fulfilled in Christ and the church.

verses.text: “Now these are the names of the tribes: From the north end, beside the way of Hethlon to the entrance of Hamath, Hazar Enan at the border of Damascus, northward beside Hamath (and they shall have their sides east and west), Dan, one portion.
verses.arminianNotes:
“Now these are the names of the tribes.” The list begins at the north end, by Hethlon and Hamath, with “Dan, one portion.” Arminian readers note that Dan, once at the northern edge, is placed there again.

The border names repeat those of 47:15–17.
verses.reformedNotes:
Reformed readers likewise see the order of the tribes set by the LORD.

Shared ground: both traditions read the list as the fulfillment in the vision of the equal division promised in 47:14, while holding different views of how it is to be understood.

verses.text: “By the border of Dan, from the east side to the west side, Asher, one portion.
verses.arminianNotes:
“By the border of Dan, from the east side to the west side, Asher, one portion.” Arminian readers note the simple pattern of equal strips.

Each tribe’s portion runs the width of the land.
verses.reformedNotes:
Reformed readers likewise see order and fairness in the arrangement.

Shared ground: both traditions read the repeated formula as emphasizing that each tribe receives its share, without attaching symbolism to Asher’s position.

verses.text: “By the border of Asher, from the east side even to the west side, Naphtali, one portion.
verses.arminianNotes:
“By the border of Asher, from the east side even to the west side, Naphtali, one portion.” Arminian readers note that the northern tribes are listed in turn.

Some observe that Dan, Asher, and Naphtali descend from Jacob’s servant wives (Gen 30), though the text gives no reason for the order.
verses.reformedNotes:
Reformed readers likewise hold such observations lightly.

Shared ground: both traditions agree that the text does not explain the order and read the verse as part of the orderly division of the land.

verses.text: “By the border of Naphtali, from the east side to the west side, Manasseh, one portion.
verses.arminianNotes:
“By the border of Naphtali, from the east side to the west side, Manasseh, one portion.” Arminian readers note that Manasseh receives one of Joseph’s two portions (47:13).

The earlier division of Manasseh across the Jordan is not repeated.
verses.reformedNotes:
Reformed readers likewise see the promise to Joseph kept.

Shared ground: both traditions read the verse as part of the tribal list and note the double portion of Joseph without pressing further meaning.

verses.text: “By the border of Manasseh, from the east side to the west side, Ephraim, one portion.
verses.arminianNotes:
“By the border of Manasseh, from the east side to the west side, Ephraim, one portion.” Arminian readers note that Ephraim, once the leading northern tribe, is simply one among the others.

The old division between north and south is not in view.
verses.reformedNotes:
Reformed readers likewise see a reunited people with no rival kingdoms (cf. 37:22).

Shared ground: both traditions read the equal portion of Ephraim as a sign of unity among the tribes.

verses.text: “By the border of Ephraim, from the east side even to the west side, Reuben, one portion.
verses.arminianNotes:
“By the border of Ephraim, from the east side even to the west side, Reuben, one portion.” Arminian readers note that Reuben, earlier settled east of the Jordan, now has land to the west.

The new arrangement differs from Joshua.
verses.reformedNotes:
Reformed readers likewise note the difference without harmonizing it.

Shared ground: both traditions read the verse as part of a fresh allotment of the land, holding different views of its fulfillment.

verses.text: “By the border of Reuben, from the east side to the west side, Judah, one portion.
verses.arminianNotes:
“By the border of Reuben, from the east side to the west side, Judah, one portion.” Arminian readers note that Judah, historically in the south, is placed just north of the holy portion.

The reason is not stated.
verses.reformedNotes:
Reformed readers likewise note Judah’s place next to the sanctuary and hold any explanation lightly.

Shared ground: both traditions agree that the list places the tribes around the LORD’s dwelling, with Judah and Benjamin on either side.
